options.text: Long-lived main and develop branches plus release branches
A single, always-deployable main plus short-lived feature branches merged via pull requests
No branches at all — everyone commits to their own repo

questions.explanation: GitHub Flow is lightweight: keep main always deployable, do work on short-lived branches, and merge via reviewed pull requests.

options.text: Everyone works on long-lived branches for weeks before merging
Everyone integrates into a single trunk frequently, using very short-lived branches (often behind feature flags)
A model that forbids automated testing
A GitHub-only feature for large files

questions.explanation: Trunk-based development keeps a single trunk (main) and integrates changes frequently via tiny short-lived branches, using feature flags to hide unfinished work — backed by strong CI.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Git Flow uses long-lived main and develop branches plus feature/release/hotfix branches
GitHub Flow keeps main always deployable
Conventional Commits is a commit-message convention (feat:, fix:, ...)
Trunk-based development relies on long-lived feature branches

questions.explanation: Git Flow is the structured model, GitHub Flow keeps main deployable, and Conventional Commits standardizes messages. Trunk-based development uses SHORT-lived branches with frequent integration, not long-lived ones.

questions.prompt: The commit-message convention that uses prefixes like feat: and fix: is called ______ Commits.
questions.explanation: Conventional Commits standardizes messages as type(scope): description, enabling automated changelogs and SemVer bumps.

questions.prompt: A simple web app deploys continuously, many times a day. Which workflow fits best?

options.text: Full Git Flow, for its release and develop branches
GitHub Flow or trunk-based development — lightweight and continuous
A separate long-lived branch per developer

questions.explanation: Continuous delivery favors lightweight workflows (GitHub Flow or trunk-based). Full Git Flow's develop/release/hotfix structure is overkill for an app that deploys continuously.

questions.prompt: Match each workflow/convention to its description.

pairs.right: Lightweight main + short-lived branches via PRs

questions.explanation: Git Flow is structured, GitHub Flow is lightweight, trunk-based integrates continuously, and Conventional Commits standardizes messages.
